name: XGBoost
what: A widely used version of gradient boosting.

name: Naive Bayes
what: Looks at each input on its own, asks how typical the value is for yes and for no patients, and combines the answers.

name: Random forest
what: Many decision trees, each built on a random part of the patients and inputs, voting together.

name: Linear discriminant analysis
what: Finds the weighted sum of the inputs that best separates the yes and no groups.

name: Decision tree
what: A chain of questions of the form 'is this value above a cut-off?' that ends in yes or no.

name: Gradient boosting
what: Small decision trees added one after another, each correcting the mistakes of those before.

name: Logistic regression
what: Adds up the inputs, each with a weight, and turns the sum into a chance of yes.

name: Nearest neighbours
what: Gives a patient the answer most common among the most similar patients.

name: Extra trees
what: Like a random forest, but the cut-offs are chosen at random.

name: Always no (check)
what: Not a real method: always gives the most common answer, no. It scores exactly 0.5 and checks the scoring.

name: Support vector machine, straight
what: Draws the straight dividing line between yes and no that leaves the widest gap.

name: Logistic regression, sparse
what: The same, but it can set some weights to zero, dropping those inputs.

name: Support vector machine, curved
what: The same, but the dividing line can curve.
